_comment: iter-106 WER fixture corpus. Each entry pairs a hand-curated
reference (the ground-truth transcript) with a simulated STT
hypothesis that exercises a specific error pattern. The
expected_wer_min/max bounds are tight enough to catch a
regression in the compute_wer primitive but loose enough to
survive the natural rounding of the (S+D+I)/N formula.
When a real CPU-only STT lands (faster-whisper, whisper.cpp
wrapper, etc.), the integration test can swap the simulated
hypothesis for the STT output and the same expected ranges
still apply — production-grade STT lands in 0.0-0.2 WER on
entries simulate degraded conditions that real audio fixtures
would need separate noisy-mic recordings to reproduce.

fixtures.name: clean
fixtures.description: Perfect transcription — production-grade STT on clean audio.

fixtures.name: dropped_filler
fixtures.description: STT drops the leading filler 'um' — common.
fixtures.reference: um what is the weather today

fixtures.name: noisy
fixtures.reference: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog
fixtures.hypothesis: the quick crown fox jumped on the lazy dog

fixtures.name: catastrophic
fixtures.description: STT misheard the entire utterance — every word wrong.

_audio_comment: iter-117 audio fixtures. Each entry is a real .wav file
(generated via espeak-ng) plus the reference transcript.
The integration test loads faster-whisper, transcribes the
audio, and asserts WER lands in the expected band.
espeak-ng output isn't natural speech, so the WER bands are
more permissive than what production-grade STT would do on
real recordings. Tightening the bands later (when real
human-recorded fixtures land) is a follow-up.

audio_fixtures.name: clean_audio
audio_fixtures.description: Short utterance via espeak-ng + faster-whisper round-trip.

audio_fixtures.name: quick_brown_fox_audio
audio_fixtures.reference: the quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog

audio_fixtures.name: noisy_audio
audio_fixtures.description: iter-124: clean speech + gaussian noise at ~15 dB SNR (deterministic seed=42). Tests faster-whisper noise tolerance against real audio rather than simulated hypotheses (iter-106 'noisy' band).

audio_fixtures.name: catastrophic_audio
audio_fixtures.description: iter-125: clean speech + gaussian noise at ~10 dB SNR (deterministic seed=42). At this SNR the tiny model fails — observed transcript 'what in the web of the May' (WER 1.0). Validates iter-106's 'catastrophic' band against real degraded audio.
